subject: POC: FintechX trial planning - workload intake & success criteria

Subject: POC: FintechX trial planning - workload intake & success criteria

Alex / Sasha — thanks again for a productive call today. Quick recap + next steps so we can get the POC scoped and scheduled. Please reply inline where you want to adjust anything.

Call recap / success criteria (as discussed)
- Primary objective: validate Redwood inference integration for FintechX real-time document summarization pipeline and ensure 95th percentile latency < 350ms at target production load.
- Functional success: generated summaries meet existing QA pass rate (internal threshold) on a stratified test set (we'll define exact evals).
- Cost target: keep per-1k-token inference cost under $X (we'll provide initial estimate after workload intake).

What we need from you (Workload intake) — please fill the attached template or paste answers:
- Representative RPS (steady-state) and expected concurrency during business hours.
- Typical and max token lengths (input prompt + expected model output).
- Burst patterns: expected spikes (RPS), duration, and frequency (daily/weekly/monthly).
- Sequence length distribution (percentiles if available) and any long-tail outliers.
- Model preference/compatibility (open model family or custom model) and target quality metrics.

Attached: workload_intake_template.xlsx — please return by EOD Tue (6/30) if possible.

Proposed timeline
- 6/30: you send workload intake + sample logs.
- 7/2: Redwood does initial capacity & cost estimate; propose POC config.
- 7/7-7/21: 2-week POC (can extend depending on results).

Owners
- Redwood AE: Marissa Cole (I’ll own coordination + success criteria).
- Redwood Solutions/Eng: Ben Carter (will lead capacity sizing & onboarding).
- FintechX technical lead: Alex Johnson (will provide logs + validate test set).

Next steps
1) Alex: send workload intake + a sample of request logs and example documents.
2) Ben: will propose an initial infra profile (GPU type, batch sizes, concurrency knobs) once we get the numbers.
3) Marissa: schedule kickoff and confirm success criteria doc.

Thanks — talk soon.
\--

Thanks Marissa — appreciate the clear recap. Quick answers below and I attached a short sample of request logs (sample_request_log.csv). We’ll fill the worksheet but wanted to get these high-level numbers in case you want to start sizing.

Preliminary workload profile (high-level)
- Steady-state RPS: 45 req/sec (business hours 08:00-18:00 ET)
- Peak bursts: up to ~320 req/sec for 2-4 minutes, typically 2-3x per day (coinciding with batch ingestion windows).
- Concurrency: expected backend concurrency of 40-60 active inference workers during steady state; bursts push concurrent sessions to ~200.
- Typical token lengths: input prompts ~60-150 tokens; expected model output 120-300 tokens (summary length varies by doc).
- Max observed token length in logs: ~2,400 tokens (very rare, <0.1% of requests).
- Sequence length distribution: P50 ~220 tokens, P90 ~520 tokens, P99 ~1100 tokens.

Other notes:
- We prefer to test on an open LLM (GPT-style family) with quantized/FP16 variants — open to your recommendations.
- We can share a ~1k-row sample evaluation set for quality checks.

I’ll upload the completed intake by EOD Tue (6/30). Let us know if you need different timezones for scheduling.

Alex
Alex Johnson
Engineering Manager, Data Platform | FintechX
alex.johnson@fintechx.com

Attachments: sample_request_log.csv

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Re: POC: FintechX trial planning - workload intake & success criteria

Appreciate the quick numbers, Alex — very helpful. A few quick thoughts from the sizing side:

Initial sizing assumptions (rough)
- To hit P95 <350ms at steady 45 RPS with P90 token lengths ~520: recommend starting with 2 x A100-like instances with Redwood Dedicated config (continuous batching + KV caching enabled).
- For burst tolerance to 320 RPS (short windows) we should enable autoscale + burst capacity (pre-warm 1-2 GPUs) and tune batching window to avoid latency regressions.
- For very long requests (2.4k tokens), we’ll route those to a slower batch/async pipeline or use a model variant with better long-context performance to avoid impacting low-latency traffic.

Success criteria / eval plan (tentative)
- Perf: P95 latency < 350ms on the steady-state test harness (synthetic replay of logs).
- Quality: summary pass rate >= current FintechX baseline on stratified eval set (we’ll define metrics and thresholds).
- Reliability: no more than 1% error rate during 2-week POC under realistic replay.

Action items
- Alex: share sample logs + 1k evaluation rows (you said you’ll upload by 6/30).
- Marissa: confirm success criteria doc & schedule kickoff (propose Mon 7/5 or Tue 7/6).
- Rishi: can you take lead on infra sizing and prepare an initial config + cost estimate by 7/2?

I’ll draft a runbook for replaying logs into the POC infra once we have the logs.

-Ben
